explanation: Matches erdosproblems.com/483: with f(k) the least N such that every k-colouring of {1,…,N} has a monochromatic solution of a + b = c (Schur numbers, f(1) = 2, f(2) = 5, …), 'is it true that f(k) < c^k for some constant c > 0?' The Lean statement: ∃ C > 0 such that for every k ≥ 1 there is N < C^k with Forces k N (every χ : Fin N → Fin k has a, b, c with a + b = c, values shifted to {1,…,N}, all of one colour, a = b allowed). Since Forces k N is monotone in N (restrict a colouring of a longer interval), the existence of some N < C^k with Forces k N is equivalent to f(k) < C^k, as the docstring notes; allowing a = b matches the Schur-number convention (f(1) = 2 via 1+1 = 2, checked by the test). Faithful.
